subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Surgical Sterilisation, Pomeroy Tubectomy and Vasectomy

steps.tx: Permanent surgical contraception for women is achieved through **female tubal sterilization**. Accomplished via minilaparotomy, laparoscopy, or during cesarean delivery, the procedure interrupts bilateral fallopian tube continuity to prevent ovum pickup and sperm transit. Pre-procedure counselling must emphasize the permanent, irreversible nature of the intervention.
steps.say: Tubal sterilization permanently interrupts the fallopian tubes to prevent fertilization.

vis.alt: Female tubal ligation and surgical techniques.
vis.caption: Permanent female sterilization following bilateral mid-isthmic tubal ligation. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The most widely performed open sterilization technique worldwide is the **modified Pomeroy technique**. Performed through a subumbilical minilaparotomy postpartum or suprapubic incision in interval cases, the mid-isthmic loop of the fallopian tube is elevated, its base ligated with plain or chromic catgut suture, and the knuckle of the loop excised.
steps.say: The Pomeroy technique ligates an elevated loop of mid-isthmic tube with absorbable suture and excises it.

left.title: Pomeroy Step Sequence
points: Loop excised leaving two open lumens

right.title: Healing Cascade
points: Cut ends pull apart and retract spontaneously
Lumen fibroses closed with low recanalisation risk

steps.tx: A vital technical principle of the Pomeroy procedure is the strict use of **absorbable suture material**. Non-absorbable silk or braided polyester must never be used to ligate the loop base because non-absorbable sutures cut through tissue, predisposing to tuboperitoneal fistula formation, chronic pelvic pain, and catastrophic ectopic pregnancy.
steps.say: Absorbable catgut allows the divided ends to separate cleanly, preventing tuboperitoneal fistulas.

rows: Absorbs as ends fibrose and pull apart

steps.tx: Laparoscopic tubal occlusion frequently employs spring-loaded **silastic Falope rings**. Applied via a specialized dual-channel applicator, a loop of mid-isthmic fallopian tube is drawn into an inner cylinder and a stretched silicone ring is slipped over its base. The ring exerts continuous compressive ischemia, leading to avascular necrosis and permanent fibrotic division.
steps.say: Falope rings exert compressive ischemia on a knuckle of tube to achieve permanent fibrotic division.

vis.alt: Falope ring tubal occlusion device and silicone band.
vis.caption: Falope ring applicator and silastic band occluding the mid-isthmic fallopian tube. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: When pregnancy occurs following tubal sterilisation, the patient faces a markedly elevated **ectopic pregnancy risk**. While sterilization drastically reduces absolute pregnancy rates, approximately one-third of post-sterilization failures represent ectopic tubal implantations resulting from microscopic recanalisation or tuboperitoneal fistulas. Any amenorrhoea or acute pelvic pain mandates urgent pregnancy testing.
steps.say: One-third of post-sterilization pregnancies are ectopic due to microscopic recanalization.

left.title: Post-Sterilization Failure Profile
points: Overall failure rate approx 2 to 5 per 1000
Higher in younger women with active fertility
Peak failure occurs 2 to 3 years post-procedure

right.title: Ectopic Proportion
points: 30 to 40 percent of failures are ectopic
Impaired ciliary transit traps blastocyst in tube

steps.tx: The definitive surgical sterilization procedure for males is **bilateral vasectomy**. Accomplished under local infiltration via conventional incisional surgery or the minimally invasive no-scalpel vasectomy technique, both vasa deferentia are isolated, divided, and occluded via luminal cautery, ligation, or fascial interposition to halt the passage of testicular spermatozoa.
steps.say: Vasectomy surgically divides the vas deferens to prevent sperm entry into the ejaculate.

vis.alt: Vasectomy surgical pathway and male reproductive anatomy.
vis.caption: Vasectomy surgical isolation, division and occlusion of the bilateral vas deferens. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Developed by Dr Li Shunqiang, the **no-scalpel vasectomy technique** utilizes two specialized instruments: an extracutaneous ringed fixation clamp and a sharp curved dissecting forceps. By puncturing rather than incising the scrotal skin, the no-scalpel approach dramatically decreases intraoperative bleeding, hematoma formation, wound infection, and postoperative convalescence time.
steps.say: The no-scalpel vasectomy punctures scrotal skin to minimize hematoma and infection risks.

rows: Single midline puncture with dissecting forceps
One or two scrotal knife incisions

steps.tx: Vasectomy does not confer immediate sterility because viable spermatozoa remain stored in the distal ampulla and seminal vesicles, requiring **post-vasectomy semen analysis**. Patients must use alternative contraception until semen analysis performed at twelve weeks and after at least twenty ejaculates confirms azoospermia or rare non-motile sperm.
steps.say: Backup contraception is required until semen analysis at twelve weeks confirms complete azoospermia.

left.title: Clearance Protocol
points: Clears residual stored sperm in ampulla

right.title: Azoospermia Criteria
points: Semen analysis confirms zero motile sperm
Unprotected intercourse permitted only after clearance
